chapter: Auditions, musicians and the jazz club
title: Band auditions and rehearsals
summary: Steinau attended auditions more than rehearsals, including Billie and De De Pierce, a Lutton's group and Emile Barnes in the record shop.

bands.name: Billie and De De Pierce's group

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Well, they certainly didn't mind doing it. I think at times they didn't have many jobs, even people like Joyce Lewis. Yeah. There was a chance for them to get together and play. That's true. It certainly wasn't a rehearsal. No, it wasn't. Did you go to rehearsals ever?

I don't, I probably have gone to a rehearsal. I've gone more to auditions than I have to a rehearsal. Yeah. I know on several occasions I was notified by one person or another that a particular group, well, it seems to me that you had one for Billy. Billy and Dee Dee Pierce and their group in the back of the New Orleans record shop. I'll pass the leader.
I'll pass the leader. We got the tape on there.
And we were talking about the Billy and Dee Dee Pierce audition. Yeah, well.

Well, I actually said all I had to say about that one. I also went to one out at, and this is on some of the earlier tapes, out at Lentons on Airline Highway, which had Eddie Pearson, Joe Thomas, who else was in that group? I think Alvin Alcorn. I think Alvin Alcorn. It might have been Paul Barberman's band.
It sounds like I think we went through this before.
That sounds like Emil Barnes' band auditioning in the back of the record shop.

You don't remember when that was. That would have been in, yes, I can. I do remember. That would probably have been in, after the first of the year, well, let's say spring of 1950. 1950 would be my guess. And who were they auditioning for? I don't know who it was. They were auditioning for somebody. It may have just been that they were auditioning for you and Oren, maybe. I don't think so. There was somebody they were auditioning for, but I don't remember the name. I think they auditioned once for Myron. That may have been. And I came late and missed a lot. There were a lot of it that were really good.
Ralston was there one time when they auditioned. Sounds right. And, of course, he was always taking pictures. When he had any opportunity, he was dedicated to that.

When you went to Lulee White's, did you get any pieces of marrow? No. I got, I think, two pieces, two small panes, about four by four inches. Of very fancy bathroom window glass. And some pieces of wallpaper. Mm-hmm. Still have both. Yeah.
